relevance_note: Family report of two patients with a TNFAIP3 variant: "a heterozygous NM_001270508.2: c.608T > G, p.(Leu203Arg) missense variant of TNFAIP3 in both patients".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script from values I typed (no automated table transcription). Table 1 has patients as rows (P1, P2); P1's row is split across two Markdown lines inside the Igs cell, so P1 table spans quote the cell text only. Scope: P1 (mother), P2 (daughter), the brother of P1 (affected relative described in the Figure 1 legend; not tested) and L001, a CVID patient used as a control in the functional assays who is stated to carry a TNFAIP3 LoF variant (individual-level variant and A20/actin ratio given; included under the TNFAIP3-variant scope rule). The heterozygous TNFRSF13B c.310T > C (p.Cys104Arg) variant in P1 is described as 'a known risk factor' present in 0.3%-0.5% of the population, so it was left out under the risk-allele rule (the Discussion also says it may contribute to IgA deficiency and autoimmunity in the mother). No variant row for the brother (no testing reported). P2 inheritance recorded as inherited maternal because the paper states the same variant is in both patients and P1 is her mother; P1 inheritance not reported. Age at presentation (P1 49 years, P2 29 years) is not last evaluation or diagnosis age; it is recorded only as onset of the presenting features. Age at HA20 diagnosis not stated. Possible inconsistencies: Table 1 gives P1 age at onset '18 years' while the text reports a childhood history of oral and genital ulcers; Table 1 gives P2 onset '9 years' while the text says ulcers since adolescence. P1's CT angiography was 'without features typical of vasculitis' but a skin biopsy showed leucocytoclastic vasculitis; not treated as a person-level contradiction (different vessels/methods), vasculitis checklist observed. Gastroenteritis (P1, a single bout with high fever) and diarrhea (P2) were not counted as gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation; leukopenia (P1) was not counted as autoimmune cytopenia since the paper does not call it autoimmune; P2 'no signs of insulin deficiency' left type 1 diabetes not reported; brother's 'rheumatism' and 'thyroid disease' were not mapped to checklist items. No stacked (' / ') cells occur in this paper. is_proband left null for P1 and P2 (neither is called proband or index case).
